client_brief:
Corner & Cure: Cold case label run

Project overview
Corner & Cure is the repeat client for this benchmark series. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Cold case label run, Corner & Cure counter photography, Recovered Corner & Cure sign, and Marketplace item tile set.

What we will provide
cornerandcure_counter_shots/ (18 phone frames); cornerandcure_board_sign.jpg; cornerandcure_label_press.pdf; cornerandcure_items.csv (38 rows); cornerandcure_brand_note.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Cold case label run: The label printer's press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the item list: the printer's run with page count equal to row count in roster...
- Corner & Cure counter photography: Eighteen phone frames brought to one warm counter look, one warmth, one black point and one sense of how close the food sits, plus one licensed camera scale frame graded into the same world so it can carry the window piece. 
- Recovered Corner & Cure sign: The hand painted board recovered as placeable scalable cutting artwork with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the knife device present beside the word, delivered as a single colour cutting version...
- Marketplace item tile set: Item tiles knocked onto the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds where food meets wrapping paper under close inspection rather than at thumbnail scale, with the...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$3,000-$7,000 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a scrappy New York style sandwich shop needing storefront art for a delivery ordering app, asking for something 'gritty, bold, and a little chaotic', 'not polished or corporate', and saying 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image'. The real shop is named in the post, so it is laundered to the coined fictional Corner & Cure and the marketplace is genericised. Co-anchors: the Upwork post from a family owned neighbourhood restaurant wanting static paid social creative for two recurring offers, personality stated as 'authentic, community-focused, family-oriented, warm, bold, local neighborhood favorite' and explicitly not a corporate chain, laundered to a fictional operator; and the Freelancer.com post for a fast food counter wanting a 'creative, vibrant, and appetizing' menu in a 'retro, street-food, rustic chalkboard' style with room for photography and print ready output. The ledger's verdict is REBUILD because the original concept sat almost entirely on one authoring surface. The honest fuller commission is what all three clients are really buying: one warm counter look pulled out of their own phone pictures, their own hand painted sign recovered as artwork rather than redrawn, and that material carried onto the window, the wall, the cold case and the daily posts.

price_band_and_audience: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl, walk up neighbourhood trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, decided in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. The band is load bearing. At impulse pricing the food is shown warm, saturated and cropped close enough to read across a room, the boards are dense but scannable, the price is set at tile size in the display face because the price is the offer, and the whole thing carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid. Treat the same photographs the way the sibling tasting room commission is correctly treated, dark grounds, one dish a page, price whispered at body size, and a twelve dollar sandwich shop reads as pretentious and empty. Push the other way into starbursts and four fonts and it reads as a franchise nobody trusts with a sandwich. A posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Sandwiches worth leaving the block for.
brand_identity.sector: A fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a cold case and a marketplace storefront, on a corner in Brooklyn, New York.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Brooklyn, New York; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Corner & Cure is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Brooklyn, New York, and this commission covers phase 2: counter refit, cold-case labels and signage.
brand_identity.audience: Walk up trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, deciding in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. They want appetite and honesty, not polish.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl. Impulse priced but not cheap: the price is the offer and sits large and proud, while the whole shop works to look like a place that is worth it rather than a bargain or a franchise.
brand_identity.typography: The hand painted board sign carries the name and sets the tone. Around it, a bold condensed display face for the wall board, prices and specials, prices at tile size so they read across the room, with a plain workhorse sans for hours, loyalty rules and small print. Warm and loud, never a novelty pile.
brand_identity.voice: Plainspoken, neighbourhood, a little brash and generous. Example line the brand would write: 'Pulled together, piled high, see you at the counter.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no digital version of the sign: the name survives only as a board hand painted by a sign painter twenty years ago and screwed to the wall over the slicer. Everything else was shot on the owner's phone over the counter. A two page written note holds the voice, hours, loyalty rules and section names, and the label printer holds a press file.
brand_identity.values: A family corner shop, second generation. Real food for regulars, made with the hand of a place, not a chain.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_counter_shots/ (18 phone frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photography shot by the owner over the counter across several weeks, food on the shop's own butcher paper, mixed daylight and strip light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have. Shot on my phone on the paper we wrap on. Some at lunch, some late afternoon."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The butcher paper sits at almost the same value as a toasted crust, so on an unknown subset of frames a one call knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout that has quietly bitten the crust edge where the two meet, and the bite is invisible until the cutout is placed on the marketplace's flat ground. The frames are also phone scale, so nothing cut from them can carry a large format window piece, and three of the eighteen are the same sandwich shot on three different days.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_board_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the hand painted name board over the slicer, shot at an angle under tungsten: brush drawn letters with hairline joins, plus a small painted knife device beside the word.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our sign. My father had it painted twenty years ago and there is no file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The painted letterforms carry hairline brush joins and small counters that a trace holds comfortably at full canvas and closes at the height the window actually reproduces the mark, on the actual glass colour rather than on white. It is also a compound lockup, so a selection naming the whole sign returns the word and silently drops the knife device, and paint and aged board run close in value across the shadowed half of the board.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_label_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the label printer supplied for the cold case shelf label: a small landscape label carrying an item name, a size line, a price roundel and a dietary tag strip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label our printer already runs. This is his file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed label reads as four separate blocks with a picture well in the roundel, but the roundel is a decorative element rather than a picture frame and the name, size and price were set as one continuous flow, so the frame inventory the conversion exposes is nothing like the printed label suggests. The file carries no bleed, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_items.csv (38 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The cold case item list: item name, size, price, dietary tags and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything in the case. This is the list we print off."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three items were never photographed and their picture cells are simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, and two items share a name at two different sizes, so naming one file per item by name collides and silently overwrites.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_brand_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages the owner wrote: the voice, the hours, the loyalty rules, the section names for the wall board and a note that the specials change daily.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk and what goes where. The specials change every day, so we have to be able to swap them."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where the food meets the paper it is sitting on. The shop wraps on butcher paper and photographs on it, and on an unknown subset of frames the paper sits at almost the value of a toasted crust. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where crust and paper share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each photograph's own light, not of the sandwich, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result has been looked at on the ground it will sit on, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the food was shot on the paper they wrap on. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the wrapping paper, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route per frame, re-derive the affected tiles through the selection and fill chain, and re-inspect every tile against the marketplace's actual flat ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A marketplace storefront where the hero sandwiches have a chewed edge along the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on the one surface where a customer decides in six seconds.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered sign is still the sign at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the word is there, the brush drawn letterforms are there, the counters are open, and at full canvas on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The window company puts it on the glass at about a hand's width tall across a dark painted band, and at that height on that ground the hairline brush joins fill in and the small counters close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the window. Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork the window company can cut and says the mark has to still be their sign. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster on a different route, re-trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re-place the result at reproduction height on the real ground and re-judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Vinyl cut and applied to the window in which the family name reads as a row of solid shapes, which is both the most visible piece in the refit and the one that cannot be quietly reprinted.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered label proof actually contains the record its filename claims. The natural way to give counter staff a proof per item is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are wrong: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster, and nothing in the response says so. Every gate above it passes, the count is right, each file is a valid label, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the item name and price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right item's own price is the shop's requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page run whose page order is trustworthy or a per record run producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re-run the cold case set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, and re-check the two items that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A cold case where the price under the turkey is the price of the roast beef, printed, laminated and clipped into the rail, discovered by a customer rather than by the shop.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the shop edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the eighteen frames are one shop, and how far to push the strip light frames before they stop being worth saving.
Knockout route per frame, between the one call route and a material named selection of the wrapping paper inverted and filled, where food and paper share value.
Where the window poster hero comes from, given nothing cut from a phone frame can carry it and enlargement is not an option.
Whether the single colour cutting version or the colour accurate variant is what the window company actually needs, judged at reproduction height on the glass colour.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an impulse band and a hand painted sign it must sit beside, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What a label for an item with no photograph looks like, decided before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
Which delivery route carries per record identity safely, and what key names a file when two items share a name.

verifier_contract.ranking_rule: Rank agents first on host-neutral final artifacts. Report connector completion and normalized process quality as separate dimensions.

artifact_checks.text: The delivery manifest contains every scoped deliverable and no undeclared substitute.
artifact_checks.how: Match the manifest against these exact deliverable names: Cold case label run; Corner & Cure counter photography; Recovered Corner & Cure sign; Marketplace item tile set.

artifact_checks.text: Every supplied input has a recorded disposition.

artifact_checks.text: Every marketplace item tile is exactly 1080 x 1080 px square and sits on a single flat brand ground colour at all four corners.
artifact_checks.how: Read each tile's pixel dimensions and assert both axes are exactly 1080 (a 1:1 square well below the 4032x3024 source, so no enlargement); then sample a 32x32 px patch at each of the four corners and assert all four are one identical RGB value that matches one of the five brand palette hexes (#B4382C, #D9A536, #F2E7CE, #2A2622, #4E6B3A), confirming a flat brand ground rather than photographic content at the edges.

artifact_checks.text: The recovered sign's SVG has a viewBox attribute, no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and contains geometry for both the word and the knife device.
artifact_checks.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a numeric viewBox attribute is present, assert the element at path index zero is not an axis-aligned rectangle spanning the full viewBox (no opaque full-canvas ground path), and count the top-level path groups, asserting at least two distinct groups so both the word and the knife device carry geometry.

human_craft_checks.text: The sign still reads as the family's sign at the height it goes on the glass, on the glass colour, with its counters open.
human_craft_checks.how: Place the delivered artwork at its stated reproduction height on the window's ground colour and read it at that size, not at full canvas.

human_craft_checks.text: The cut edge holds where the food meets the wrapping paper, on every tile, against the marketplace's own ground.
human_craft_checks.how: View each tile at full resolution on the flat brand ground and look along the crust and the paper boundary.

human_craft_checks.text: Every cold case label carries its own item's price and tags, including the items with no photograph.
human_craft_checks.how: Read each proof against its roster row, starting with the two items that share a name and the three with no picture.

human_craft_checks.text: The work reads as a twelve to sixteen dollar neighbourhood counter, not as a tasting room and not as a franchise.
human_craft_checks.how: Judge warmth, tile density, how large the price sits and whether the hand of the painted sign carries, against the stated band and customer.

human_craft_checks.text: The brand basis reads as something a new hire could actually run the front of house from, keeping the system consistent without repainting it.

acceptance_snapshot: The sign is placeable cutting artwork rather than a picture of a sign: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the knife device present alongside the word, and every counter still open at the height it actually goes on the glass, on the glass colour rather than on white.

Every marketplace item tile sits on the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds where the food meets the wrapping paper when looked at close up rather than at thumbnail scale.
The three social canvases sit in one working document, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source they were built from.
Prices are set at tile size in the display face and read across the room, and the whole system carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid.

The cold case run produces one label per item with the right item's own price and tags, page count equalling row count, per item files identifiable where two items share a name, and the three items with no picture handled deliberately rather than left as holes.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
Production-readiness claims are limited to geometry that can be inspected; vectorization alone is never accepted as evidence of fabrication readiness.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns appetising pictures of sandwiches and a picture of a chalkboard. IDENTITY: these are this shop's own sandwiches on this shop's own paper, and the sign is a specific hand painted board a sign painter made twenty years ago, which has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated sign is a different family's name in a different hand and the window company cuts vinyl from paths, not from a picture. SPEC: the marketplace needs tiles at an exact size on a flat ground with a cut edge that survives close inspection, the window needs a closed path that still reads at a stated height, and the cold case needs one label per item bound to that item's own price with page count equal to row count, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the specials change daily and the shop swaps them itself, so a flat picture of a board is worthless a day after delivery. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout bite the crust, does this trace hold at hand height on green, is the price inside this file the price on this row.
